study: Optimized DM Prop versus Self-Funded Capital Efficiency v1
purpose: Compare the frozen Optimized DM 63D/Daily strategy under the existing prop-account lifecycle with a same-effective-exposure self-funded account, without changing signals, execution ownership, or the frozen prop study.

propAccount.capitalCommittedDefinition: Cumulative trader-paid challenge and reset fees; nominal account capacity is not treated as trader-owned capital.
propAccount.capitalAtRiskDefinition: Cumulative non-refundable challenge and reset fees paid by the trader. Contractual rule risk and lost future opportunity are reported separately, not assigned a fabricated dollar capital base.

selfFundedComparatorA.startingAndCommittedCapital: Exactly the effective exposure: nominalAccount multiplied by scale ($20,000 or $25,000).
selfFundedComparatorA.exposure: Fixed dollar exposure equal to the matched prop exposure; no compounding of position size.
selfFundedComparatorA.returnPath: The same sampled, execution-calibrated Optimized DM daily return path used by the prop account.
selfFundedComparatorA.fees: No prop challenge/reset fees and no payout split. Strategy transaction costs and observed execution calibration remain embedded in the return path.
selfFundedComparatorA.capitalAtRiskDefinition: The self-funded account equity committed to the strategy.
selfFundedComparatorA.negativeEquityTreatment: No artificial stopout; losses continue on the fixed exposure and may exceed starting capital in a simulated extreme path.

selfFundedComparatorB.reason: No legitimate, previously preregistered personal stop/restart rule exists. A restart rule will not be invented after seeing outcomes.

simulation.sampling: Reuse the frozen study's candidate-specific seed offset and moving-block bootstrap exactly.
simulation.accountDependence: Perfectly correlated identical accounts: same strategy, same marks, same rule state, and synchronized breaches/payouts. Aggregate path metrics are computed path by path, never from multiplied summary medians.

primaryComparisons: 0.20x prop trailing-to-breakeven versus $20,000 self-funded fixed exposure
0.25x prop static versus $25,000 self-funded fixed exposure
approvedSensitivities: Static versus trailing-to-breakeven prop rules at both frozen scales
Registered historical backtest costs only versus the current observed execution overlay for Optimized DM
metrics: expected, median, 5th-percentile, and 1st-percentile annual net profit
probability of annual loss and probability of reaching $35,000 aggregate net profit
prop breach probabilities, expected resets, fees, payouts, and time to first payout
self-funded peak-to-trough drawdown and probability of crossing the equivalent $6,000 absolute loss threshold
capital committed, effective exposure, return on committed capital, and drawdown utilization
break-even available-own-capital thresholds, reported as feasibility thresholds and economic-return comparisons rather than a leverage recommendation

prospectiveExtension.source: The same append-only Alpaca paper account equity snapshots and locked execution fingerprint consumed by the existing prop shadows.
prospectiveExtension.orders: Observation only; these ledgers cannot place, modify, or cancel orders.
prospectiveExtension.start: First raw snapshot inserted after this preregistration is installed. No historical snapshot backfill.
prospectiveExtension.classification: Prospective observations remain separate from historical development and Monte Carlo results.

interpretationGuards: No strategy parameter, universe, holding, order, execution baseline, prop rule, or historical prop artifact may change.
Historical Optimized DM evidence is selection-contaminated and cannot substitute for forward evidence.
Daily OHLC envelopes are approximate for intraday rules; prospective five-minute account marks are the higher-quality evidence stream.
The $35,000 target frontier is descriptive. It does not select an account count or scale.
Nominal prop buying power is not personal capital and must not appear in return-on-capital denominators.
Perfectly correlated accounts do not diversify breach risk; probability of at least one breach equals the single-account breach probability.
No conclusion may be upgraded beyond depends-on-capital or inconclusive solely from the one-year selected development sample.
